newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay to restart HK-Chicago freight run.
newsitem.headline: Cathay to restart HK-Chicago freight run.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd plans to restart its freighter service to Chicago which it handed over to its 75 percent all-cargo subsidiary AHK Air Hong Kong Ltd nine months ago, a Cathay source told Reuters.

The relaunch is planned for June using one of the airline's two, more efficient Boeing 747-400 freighters twice a week to Chicago only and twice weekly going on to New York. The move was disclosed in a Cathay press statement earlier Monday which hailed the signing of an air services agreement between Hong Kong and the USA.

"Plans are afoot for the service to revert back to us and we're going back in there. We have learnt from experience that the route is best operated by a 747-400 which are far more economical (than 747-200s)", the source said.

"The plan on the drawing board is to effectively double the existing frequency to four times a week with two of the flights extending on to New York. The U.S. market is very strong right now in both directions," he added.

AHK was given the route last August when AHK took delivery of newly converted 747-200 aircraft leased from Cathay. Cathay Cargo said it wanted to concentrate on its new twice weekly service to New York. AHK then hailed their new service to the key U.S. gateway as a new beginning and an important milestone after heavy losses.
Industry sources said it appears the switch has not been a success.
AHK offcials were not available for comment as how AHK's freighters would now be deployed.
However the industry sources said plans to start for a new AHK service to the South Korean capital, Seoul were recently mooted.
At present AHK flies to Chicago twice a week but plans to increase the service to three times weekly never materialised. Last October, the airline's former head blamed a shortage of trained crew.
